scenarios.query:
Review this design excerpt from an internal-platform RFC:

> To keep the data model flexible as the domain evolves, all entity types (Order, User, Invoice, Shipment) will share one `Entity` class with a single `attributes: dict[str, Any]` bag instead of per-type fields. Any code that needs a specific attribute reads it out of the dict by key at the point of use.
expected_behavior: Flags that this design makes illegal states trivially representable: nothing stops an Order-shaped dict from missing required fields, holding fields that belong to a different entity type, or holding an internally inconsistent combination

Flags primitive obsession at scale: every domain concept collapses into stringly-keyed dict lookups with no compile-time or construction-time guarantee of shape, deferring all validation to each call site
Recommends per-type value objects/records (or a tagged union if there's real shared behavior) instead of one untyped attribute bag
Applies this judgment to the RFC prose itself, not just a code diff

Recommends either giving it real behavior (translating to/from domain objects, centralizing query logic) or removing the wrapper

scenarios.query:
Review this change:
```python
class ShoppingCart:
    def __init__(self):
        self._items = []
    def items(self):
        return self._items   # returns the live internal list
```
```python
cart.items().append(rogue_item)   # bypasses ShoppingCart's own add_item() validation
```
expected_behavior: Flags that items() returns a reference to the cart's own internal mutable list, so any caller can mutate the cart's contents directly and bypass whatever invariants add_item() is meant to enforce (stock checks, dedup, limits)
Recommends returning a copy or an immutable view (tuple / frozen collection) so mutation stays behind an explicit method

scenarios.query:
Review this change:
```python
class ReportBuilder:
    def open(self): ...
    def configure(self, options): ...
    def build(self): ...
```
```python
builder = ReportBuilder()
builder.build()   # never called open()/configure() -- nothing prevents this
```
expected_behavior: Flags that nothing in the type signature prevents calling build() before open()/configure() — the required call sequence is documented, not enforced
Notes the caller in the example skips both steps and gets an unclear crash or a subtly wrong report as a result

Recommends a design that makes the invalid sequence unrepresentable (e.g. a builder that returns a differently-typed object at each stage, or a single factory taking everything needed up front) rather than relying on callers reading the docs
Flags the recurring (street, city, zip_code) parameter cluster traveling together across three functions as a Data Clump
Recommends extracting an Address value type and passing that instead, so the relationship between the three fields is named and enforced once rather than repeated at every call site
Flags that Square extends Rectangle purely to reuse area(), but has to override both setters to keep width/height in lockstep
Notes a Square is not substitutable for a Rectangle: setting only width silently changes height too, breaking any code that treats a Rectangle as independently resizable (an LSP violation)
Recommends composition (a shared Shape interface both implement independently) over an inheritance relationship that doesn't actually hold
